description.value: The study examined whether chronic smoking and acute nicotine administration alter reward-related temporal difference error activity in mesocorticolimbic and nigrostriatal regions.

spans.text: Using a classical conditioning paradigm, we observed outcomes indicative of trait effects of being a dependent smoker but not state effects of acute nicotine administration in TDE/reward-related activity in regions along the trajectory of MCL and NS DA pathways.

value: We hypothesized that acute administration of nicotine and chronic exposure to nicotine in dependent smokers would modify TDE processing of a natural reward.

description.value: Dependent smokers and matched control subjects were scanned in two sessions; smokers received nicotine or placebo patches and control subjects were scanned without patch manipulation.

### Temporal Difference Error/Juice Paradigm

description.value: Participants were exposed to training/normal events and catch trials involving a visual cue and juice reward.

spans.text: During experimental runs, participants were exposed to training/normal trials ( n = 58) interspersed with randomly selected catch trials ( n = 20; B), wherein the juice reward was unpredictably and pseudorandomly delayed by 4 to 7 seconds.

There were four regressors of interest: light cue (CS), normal events (unconditioned stimulus [UCS]; juice expected/juice delivered), NTDE (juice expected/juice not delivered), and PTDE (juice not expected/juice delivered).

description.value: Conditioned-stimulus event: presentation of the yellow light cue that predicted juice delivery after a 6-second delay.

instructions.value: Participants learned to associate a yellow light cue with delayed juice delivery. During the timing task, they indicated whether the final tone interval was shorter than, longer than, or equal to the preceding intervals; they also rated juice liking after each task block.
